\title{Problem Sheet for Iteris: Energy Functionals for 2D Maxwell--PML}
\author{Prepared source problem}
\date{\today}

\begin{document}
\maketitle

\begin{abstract}
This note is a self-contained source problem for an Iteris run.  The system to be analyzed is the two-dimensional TM Maxwell--PML model with polarization \(P\), PML auxiliary variables \(P_{z,1},P_{z,2},Q_x,Q_y\), and perfectly conducting boundary condition.  The first target is to find a genuinely monotone decreasing energy functional in two space dimensions.  If such a monotone energy cannot be found, the fallback target is to find a positive energy functional that proves boundedness/no abnormal long-time growth, in the same spirit as the long-time-stability role of MPML.  The non-fractional case should be understood as the special case \(\alpha=1\) of the displayed polarization law.
\end{abstract}

\section{Primary Goal}

Let \(\Om\subset\R^2\) be a rectangular computational domain containing a physical region and a PML layer.  The absorption parameters are
\[
  \sx=\sx(x)\ge0,\qquad \sy=\sy(y)\ge0,
\]
or, in a harder variant,
\[
  \sx=\sx(x,y)\ge0,\qquad \sy=\sy(x,y)\ge0.
\]
The main goal is to analyze the two-dimensional system in Section~\ref{sec:model} and construct an energy functional \(\Ecal(t)\).

\begin{enumerate}
\item \textbf{Strong target: monotone decreasing energy.}
Find a positive energy functional such that
\[
  \frac{\dd}{\dd t}\Ecal(t)=-\Dcal(t)\le0.
\]
This is the preferred outcome.
\item \textbf{Fallback target: bounded/non-growing energy.}
If no monotone energy can be found, find a positive energy functional that rules out abnormal growth from the PML layer, for example
\[
  \Ecal(t)\le C\,\Ecal(0)
\]
with \(C\) independent of long time if possible.  If only a Gronwall estimate
\[
  \frac{\dd}{\dd t}\Ecal(t)\le C_\sigma\Ecal(t)
\]
is available, identify the precise terms responsible for the possible growth and whether they are coefficient-gradient terms, corner-PML terms, or algebraic sign-indefinite terms.
\item \textbf{Useful obstruction.}
If the strong target fails for natural quadratic energies, prove or at least sharply identify the obstruction.  An obstruction result is valuable if it explains which part of the PML coupling prevents monotonicity.
\end{enumerate}

The energy may include weighted \(L^2\) norms, cross terms, shifted variables, time-integrated auxiliary variables, polarization energy, fractional-memory energy, and derivative terms if they are mathematically justified.

\section{Model to Analyze}
\label{sec:model}

The model is the system shown in the supplied manuscript image.  Write
\[
  E=E_z,\qquad \epsilon_\infty=\epsilon_{r,\infty},\qquad
  \epsilon_s=\epsilon_{r,s},\qquad \mu=\mu_0\mu_r,
\]
and
\[
  \chi=\epsilon_0(\epsilon_s-\epsilon_\infty).
\]
The unknowns are
\[
  E,\quad H_x,\quad H_y,\quad P,\quad P_{z,1},\quad P_{z,2},\quad Q_x,\quad Q_y.
\]
The PML system is
\begin{equation}
\begin{aligned}
\epsilon_0\epsilon_\infty\,\partial_t E
&= \partial_xH_y-\partial_yH_x
   -\epsilon_\infty(\sx+\sy)E
   -\partial_tP-\frac{\sx+\sy}{\epsilon_0}P
   +P_{z,1}+P_{z,2},\\
\mu\,\partial_tH_x
&= -\partial_yE-\mu\frac{\sy-\sx}{\epsilon_0}H_x+Q_x,\\
\mu\,\partial_tH_y
&= \partial_xE-\mu\frac{\sx-\sy}{\epsilon_0}H_y+Q_y,\\
P+\tau^\alpha\partial_t^\alpha P
&=\chi E,\\
\partial_tP_{z,1}
&=-\frac{\epsilon_\infty}{\epsilon_0}\sx\sy E,\\
\partial_tP_{z,2}
&=-\frac{\sx\sy}{\epsilon_0^2}P,\\
\partial_tQ_x
&=-\frac{\sx}{\epsilon_0}Q_x
  +\frac{\mu\sx(\sy-\sx)}{\epsilon_0^2}H_x,\\
\partial_tQ_y
&=-\frac{\sy}{\epsilon_0}Q_y
  +\frac{\mu\sy(\sx-\sy)}{\epsilon_0^2}H_y.
\end{aligned}
\label{eq:main-model}
\end{equation}
Here \(\partial_t^\alpha\) should be interpreted as a Caputo-type fractional derivative when \(0<\alpha<1\).  The non-fractional case requested by the user is the case
\[
  \alpha=1,\qquad
  P+\tau\partial_tP=\chi E.
\]
Thus the first stage of the analysis should use \(\alpha=1\), not a model with \(P\) removed.

The boundary condition is the perfectly conducting boundary condition
\[
  \widehat n\times E=0\qquad\text{on }\partial\Om.
\]
For the two-dimensional TM model this should be interpreted as
\[
  E=E_z=0\qquad\text{on }\partial\Om,
\]
so that the Maxwell principal part has no positive boundary contribution.  If a proof uses a different boundary condition, it must state that choice explicitly.

\begin{remark}
The parameters \(\epsilon_0,\epsilon_\infty,\epsilon_s,\mu,\tau\) are positive, and \(\chi>0\) when \(\epsilon_s>\epsilon_\infty\).  The absorption parameters are time-independent and nonnegative.  The first serious cases to analyze are constant \(\sx,\sy\), then separated variable coefficients \(\sx(x),\sy(y)\), and only then general \(\sx(x,y),\sy(x,y)\).
\end{remark}

\section{First Energy Balance to Verify}

Start with the electromagnetic part
\[
  \Ecal_{\rm em}(t)=\frac12\int_\Om
  \left(\epsilon_0\epsilon_\infty E^2+\mu H_x^2+\mu H_y^2\right)\dd x\dd y.
\]

\begin{task}[Check the electromagnetic energy derivative]
Using \eqref{eq:main-model} and the PEC boundary condition, verify that the Maxwell principal part cancels by integration by parts, and that
\[
\begin{aligned}
\frac{\dd}{\dd t}\Ecal_{\rm em}
=\int_\Om\Big[
&-\epsilon_\infty(\sx+\sy)E^2
-E\partial_tP
-\frac{\sx+\sy}{\epsilon_0}EP
+E(P_{z,1}+P_{z,2})\\
&-\frac{\mu}{\epsilon_0}(\sy-\sx)H_x^2
-\frac{\mu}{\epsilon_0}(\sx-\sy)H_y^2
+H_xQ_x+H_yQ_y
\Big]\dd x\dd y .
\end{aligned}
\label{eq:em-balance}
\]
The terms involving \(H_x,H_y\) are sign-indefinite when \(\sx\ne\sy\).  The terms involving \(P,P_{z,1},P_{z,2}\) are the electric/PML auxiliary coupling terms that must be absorbed by a refined energy.
\end{task}

\section{The \texorpdfstring{\(\alpha=1\)}{alpha=1} Polarization Identity}

For the non-fractional case \(\alpha=1\),
\[
  P+\tau\partial_tP=\chi E,
\]
so
\[
  E=\frac{P+\tau\partial_tP}{\chi}.
\]
This gives the useful identity
\begin{equation}
  E\,\partial_tP
  =\frac{1}{2\chi}\frac{\dd}{\dd t}\|P\|_{L^2(\Om)}^2
   +\frac{\tau}{\chi}\|\partial_tP\|_{L^2(\Om)}^2.
\label{eq:alpha-one-dissipation}
\end{equation}

\begin{task}[Use the alpha=1 identity]
Use \eqref{eq:alpha-one-dissipation} to decide whether the energy
\[
  \Ecal_{\rm em+P}
  =\Ecal_{\rm em}+\frac{1}{2\chi}\|P\|_{L^2(\Om)}^2
\]
is the right starting point.  Then identify the remaining troublesome electric auxiliary terms:
\[
  -\frac{\sx+\sy}{\epsilon_0}EP,\qquad
  E P_{z,1},\qquad
  E P_{z,2},\qquad
  \partial_tP_{z,1},\qquad
  \partial_tP_{z,2}.
\]
Try to absorb them using cross terms, shifted variables, or time-integrated variables.
\end{task}

\section{Magnetic Auxiliary Variable Shift}

Define
\[
  a_x=\frac{\sy-\sx}{\epsilon_0},\qquad
  a_y=\frac{\sx-\sy}{\epsilon_0},\qquad
  b_x=\frac{\sx}{\epsilon_0},\qquad
  b_y=\frac{\sy}{\epsilon_0}.
\]
The magnetic equations and \(Q_x,Q_y\) equations suggest the shifted variables
\[
  M_x=Q_x-\mu a_xH_x,\qquad
  M_y=Q_y-\mu a_yH_y.
\]

\begin{task}[Verify shifted magnetic identities]
Starting from \eqref{eq:main-model}, verify
\begin{equation}
\begin{aligned}
\partial_tM_x
&= a_x\,\partial_yE-\frac{\sy}{\epsilon_0}M_x,\\
\partial_tM_y
&= -a_y\,\partial_xE-\frac{\sx}{\epsilon_0}M_y.
\end{aligned}
\label{eq:magnetic-shift}
\end{equation}
Then test whether an energy written in terms of \(H_x,H_y,M_x,M_y\), rather than \(H_x,H_y,Q_x,Q_y\), has a cleaner dissipation structure.
\end{task}

\begin{remark}
If \(\sx,\sy\) are spatially variable, \eqref{eq:magnetic-shift} itself does not produce \(\partial_t\sigma\) terms, because the coefficients are time-independent.  However, integrated energy identities may produce \(\partial_x\sx\), \(\partial_y\sy\), or general \(\nabla\sigma_i\) terms after integration by parts.  These terms are likely to be one source of bounded-but-not-monotone estimates.
\end{remark}

\section{Electric PML Auxiliary Variables}

The variables \(P_{z,1}\) and \(P_{z,2}\) satisfy
\[
  \partial_tP_{z,1}=-\frac{\epsilon_\infty}{\epsilon_0}\sx\sy E,\qquad
  \partial_tP_{z,2}=-\frac{\sx\sy}{\epsilon_0^2}P.
\]
They appear in the \(E\)-equation as \(E(P_{z,1}+P_{z,2})\).  This resembles the need for time-integrated or cross-term energies in PML analyses.

\begin{task}[Handle Pz1 and Pz2]
Try the following routes:
\begin{enumerate}
\item define time-integrated variables
\[
  R_1(t)=\int_0^tP_{z,1}(s)\dd s,\qquad
  R_2(t)=\int_0^tP_{z,2}(s)\dd s;
\]
\item add cross terms such as \((E,P_{z,1})\), \((P,P_{z,2})\), or weighted combinations;
\item freeze \(\sx,\sy\) as constants and solve the pointwise Lyapunov matrix problem for the electric subsystem \((E,P,P_{z,1},P_{z,2})\);
\item identify whether the corner factor \(\sx\sy\) is the essential obstruction.
\end{enumerate}
\end{task}

\section{Baffet-Type Energy Design Clue}

Baffet--Grote--Imperiale--Kachanovska proved monotone energy decay for a second-order wave-equation PML with constant damping coefficients\cite{baffetGroteImperialeKachanovska2019}.  Their main lesson is methodological: do not start from the naive energy alone.  In two dimensions they introduce
\[
  \lambda=\nabla u+\phi,\qquad
  a=\operatorname{tr}\Gamma_1,\qquad
  b=\det\Gamma_1,
\]
and use an energy of the form
\[
  E[u,\phi]=\frac12\left(
  \|\partial_tu+a u\|^2+\|\nabla u+\phi\|^2
  +\|\phi\|^2_{a^{-1}\Gamma_1}+\|u\|^2_b\right).
\]
In three dimensions they further introduce time-integrated auxiliary variables \(\Phi,\Psi\) and a shifted variable \(q\).

\begin{task}[Translate the Baffet idea to \eqref{eq:main-model}]
Look for Maxwell--PML analogues of the following structures:
\begin{itemize}
\item shifted field variables analogous to \(\partial_tu+a u\);
\item combinations of principal variables and PML auxiliaries analogous to \(\nabla u+\phi\);
\item time-integrated variables such as \(\int_0^tP_{z,1}\dd s\), \(\int_0^tP_{z,2}\dd s\), \(\int_0^tQ_x\dd s\), \(\int_0^tQ_y\dd s\);
\item cross terms that turn \(E P_{z,1}\), \(E P_{z,2}\), \(H_xQ_x\), \(H_yQ_y\) into exact time derivatives plus nonpositive remainders.
\end{itemize}
Any candidate energy must be checked for positive definiteness and boundary contributions.
\end{task}

\section{Pointwise Lyapunov Matrix Route}

For the \(\alpha=1\) case and constant \(\sx,\sy\), use
\[
  \partial_tP=\frac{\chi E-P}{\tau}
\]
to rewrite \eqref{eq:main-model} as a first-order system for
\[
  U=(E,H_x,H_y,P,P_{z,1},P_{z,2},Q_x,Q_y)^T.
\]
After Fourier transform in space,
\[
  \partial_t\widehat U=A(\sx,\sy,k_x,k_y)\widehat U.
\]
Search for a Hermitian positive matrix \(G\) such that
\[
  G A + A^*G\le0.
\]
If such a \(G\) is independent of \(k\), it suggests a local \(L^2\) energy.  If \(G\) depends polynomially on \(k\), it suggests derivative energies.  If no positive \(G\) exists in a natural class, record the obstruction.

\begin{task}[Algebraic feasibility test]
Perform the pointwise Lyapunov search in the following order:
\begin{enumerate}
\item no PML: \(\sx=\sy=0\);
\item edge PML: \(\sx>0,\sy=0\);
\item edge PML: \(\sx=0,\sy>0\);
\item symmetric corner: \(\sx=\sy>0\);
\item asymmetric corner: \(\sx>0,\sy>0,\sx\ne\sy\).
\end{enumerate}
For each case, record whether there is an explicit positive quadratic energy, whether it is monotone, and whether the shifted variables \(M_x,M_y\) or integrated variables improve the result.
\end{task}

\section{Fractional Case \texorpdfstring{\(0<\alpha<1\)}{0<alpha<1}}

The first stage should analyze \(\alpha=1\).  Only after the \(\alpha=1\) mechanism is understood should the fractional case be considered.  For \(0<\alpha<1\), the equation
\[
  P+\tau^\alpha\partial_t^\alpha P=\chi E
\]
requires fractional-memory tools.  A possible route is to use a diffusive representation or complete monotonicity to produce a positive memory energy.

\begin{task}[Fractional memory extension]
Assuming the \(\alpha=1\) energy has been found or its obstruction understood, determine whether the fractional polarization can be added as a positive memory energy.  Do not assume the correct memory weight; derive it from the Cole--Cole law.  If the fractional part is not needed for the current goal, explicitly postpone it and keep the main theorem for \(\alpha=1\).
\end{task}

\section{Deliverables Requested from Iteris}

An Iteris run should aim to produce one of the following terminal artifacts.

\begin{enumerate}
\item A proved monotone energy identity for \eqref{eq:main-model} with \(\alpha=1\), under clearly stated assumptions.
\item A proved bounded-energy or no-abnormal-growth estimate for \eqref{eq:main-model} with \(\alpha=1\), if monotonicity is unavailable.
\item A verified obstruction showing why a natural class of quadratic energies cannot be monotone for the full two-dimensional corner PML.
\item A staged result: edge PML solved, corner PML reduced to a finite-dimensional Lyapunov condition, fractional \(0<\alpha<1\) case postponed with precise reason.
\end{enumerate}

Every result should state:
\begin{itemize}
\item exact model equations used;
\item whether \(\alpha=1\) or \(0<\alpha<1\);
\item boundary assumptions, especially how PEC is used;
\item assumptions on \(\sx,\sy\);

# Energy Design V3 Perfect Matching Report

Problem id: `2d_maxwell_pml_energy_functional_exploration`

终端 artifact: `results/energy_design_v3_perfect_matching_report.md`

## 1. Executive summary

本阶段回答的问题不是“v2 模型是否有单调能量”。这个问题在
`results/energy_design_v2_report_verified.md` 中已经验证：v2 协变阻尼
Maxwell--Debye 吸收层有正的单调能量。但 stage-3 的新问题是：这个模型是否真的是
perfectly matched layer。

结论如下。

1. v2 协变阻尼模型不是 perfectly matched。对于平面 \(x\)-界面、
\(\rho_x=\rho>0,\rho_y=0\)、Laplace 变量 \(s\) 和切向波数 \(k_y\)，物理
Maxwell--Debye 导纳 \(Y_0\) 与 v2 透射导纳 \(Y_{v2}\) 满足
\[
Y_{v2}^2-Y_0^2
=-\frac{\rho}{\mu^2}\left[
\frac{\mu\chi\tau}{(1+\tau s)(1+\tau(s+\rho))}
+\frac{k_y^2}{s^2(s+\rho)}
\right],
\]
所以反射系数
\[
R_{v2}=\frac{Y_0-Y_{v2}}{Y_0+Y_{v2}}
\]
通常不为零。失配有两个来源：Debye 极化率被从
\(\chi/(1+\tau s)\) 改成 \(\chi/(1+\tau(s+\rho))\)，并且斜入射项从
\(k_y^2/s^2\) 改成 \(k_y^2/[s(s+\rho)]\)。

2. 一个更接近标准 PML 的修复模型是 stretched-coordinate Maxwell--Debye
PML：在 Laplace 域中只把空间导数替换为 \(S_i(s)^{-1}\partial_i\)，同时保持
物理 Debye 定律
\[
(1+\tau s)\widehat P=\chi\widehat E.
\]
该模型在常系数平面界面处满足 \(\nu_+=S_x\nu_0\) 和 \(Y_+=Y_0\)，因此连续层面
perfectly matched。

3. 能量方面必须分开陈述。v2 模型有完整的单调耗散恒等式，但它不是精确匹配
PML。标准 stretched-coordinate 修复模型有精确匹配；其朴素物理能量在完整二维
ADE 形式中有符号不定的记忆耦合项，但引入 Baffet 型 time-primitive 变量
\(u_t=E,q_t=P\) 后，在常系数二维 PML 块上得到正的非增能量
\(\mathcal E_{BD}\) 和耗散恒等式。

4. 全计算区域上的“所有非零态严格衰减”不可能成立。若物理区域内
\(\sigma_x=\sigma_y=0\)，取
\[
E=0,\qquad P=0,\qquad H_x=\partial_x\phi,\qquad H_y=\partial_y\phi,
\]
其中 \(\phi\) 光滑且支撑在未阻尼物理区域内，则
\(\partial_xH_y-\partial_yH_x=0\)，这是非零磁能的定常解。任何诚实的耗散恒等式
都必须刻画这个零耗散空间。

当前最强结论是：v2 是稳定吸收层而不是 perfectly matched PML；标准
stretched-coordinate/Baffet-primitive Maxwell--Debye 模型在常系数二维块上同时给出
perfect matching 与非增耗散能量。下一篇 manuscript 不应把 v2 称为 PML。

## 3. Perfect matching criterion

设物理半空间为 \(x<0\)，PML 半空间为 \(x>0\)。取 Laplace--Fourier 模式
\[
E,H,P\sim e^{st+ik_y y+\nu x},\qquad \Re s>0.
\]
物理 Maxwell--Debye 介质满足
\[
P+\tau sP=\chi E,\qquad
\varepsilon_D(s)=\epsilon_0\epsilon_\infty+\frac{\chi}{1+\tau s}.
\]
物理方程为
\[
s\varepsilon_D(s)E=\partial_xH_y-\partial_yH_x,
\]
\[
\mu sH_x=-\partial_yE,\qquad \mu sH_y=\partial_xE.
\]
代入 \(\partial_x=\nu_0,\partial_y=ik_y\)，得到
\[
H_x=-\frac{ik_y}{\mu s}E,\qquad
H_y=\frac{\nu_0}{\mu s}E,
\]
\[
\nu_0^2=k_y^2+\mu s^2\varepsilon_D(s).
\]
物理导纳定义为
\[
Y_0=\frac{H_y}{E}=\frac{\nu_0}{\mu s}.
\]

对 \(x=0\) 界面，连续切向量为 \(E\) 与 \(H_y\)。若入射波振幅为 \(1\)，反射振幅为
\(R\)，透射振幅为 \(T\)，则
\[
1+R=T,\qquad Y_0(1-R)=Y_+T.
\]
因此
\[
R=\frac{Y_0-Y_+}{Y_0+Y_+}.
\]
perfect matching 的公式判据是
\[
\boxed{Y_+(s,k_y)=Y_0(s,k_y)\quad\text{对所有出射物理模成立}.}
\]

标准 stretched-coordinate PML 取
\[
S_x(s)=1+\frac{\sigma_x}{s}
\]
并替换
\[
\partial_x\mapsto S_x^{-1}\partial_x,
\]
同时保持 \(\varepsilon_D(s)\) 不变。于是 PML 中 \(\nu_+=S_x\nu_0\)，而
\[
Y_+=\frac{S_x^{-1}\nu_+}{\mu s}
=\frac{\nu_0}{\mu s}=Y_0.
\]
这就是本报告采用的匹配测试。

## 4. Perfect matching test for the v2 model

v2 模型为
\[
\epsilon_0\epsilon_\infty D_\rho E
=\partial_xH_y-\partial_yH_x-D_\rho P,
\]
\[
\mu(\partial_t+\rho_y)H_x=-\partial_yE,\qquad
\mu(\partial_t+\rho_x)H_y=\partial_xE,
\]
\[
P+\tau D_\rho P=\chi E,\qquad D_\rho=\partial_t+\rho,\quad
\rho=\rho_x+\rho_y.
\]

考虑 \(x\)-PML 常系数半空间：
\[
\rho_x=\rho>0,\qquad \rho_y=0.
\]
则
\[
P=\frac{\chi}{1+\tau(s+\rho)}E,\qquad
\varepsilon_\rho(s)
=\epsilon_0\epsilon_\infty+\frac{\chi}{1+\tau(s+\rho)}.
\]
Laplace--Fourier 代数系统是
\[
(s+\rho)\varepsilon_\rho(s)E=\nu H_y-ik_yH_x,
\]
\[
\mu sH_x=-ik_yE,\qquad
\mu(s+\rho)H_y=\nu E.
\]
所以
\[
H_x=-\frac{ik_y}{\mu s}E,\qquad
H_y=\frac{\nu}{\mu(s+\rho)}E,
\]
\[
\nu^2=\mu(s+\rho)^2\varepsilon_\rho(s)+k_y^2\frac{s+\rho}{s}.
\]
v2 透射导纳为
\[
Y_{v2}^2
=\frac{1}{\mu^2}\left(
\mu\varepsilon_\rho(s)+\frac{k_y^2}{s(s+\rho)}
\right).
\]
与
\[
Y_0^2
=\frac{1}{\mu^2}\left(
\mu\varepsilon_D(s)+\frac{k_y^2}{s^2}
\right)
\]
比较，得到精确失配
\[
\boxed{
Y_{v2}^2-Y_0^2
=-\frac{\rho}{\mu^2}\left[
\frac{\mu\chi\tau}{(1+\tau s)(1+\tau(s+\rho))}
+\frac{k_y^2}{s^2(s+\rho)}
\right].}
\]

因此 v2 不满足 \(Y_{v2}=Y_0\)。特别地：

- 即使 \(k_y=0\)，只要 \(\chi\tau\rho\ne0\)，Debye 极化率从
  \(\varepsilon_D(s)\) 变成 \(\varepsilon_\rho(s)\)，阻抗已改变。
- 即使 \(\chi=0\)，只要 \(k_y\ne0\)，斜入射项也从 \(k_y^2/s^2\) 变成
  \(k_y^2/[s(s+\rho)]\)。

结论：v2 的协变 Debye 阻尼有利于能量耗散，但破坏了标准 PML 的
stretched-coordinate 阻抗匹配。

# Stage-3 proof: repaired PML candidates and dissipative-energy classification

Problem id: `2d_maxwell_pml_energy_functional_exploration`

Task: `task-stage3-repaired-model-energy`

## Input fact from the matching test

The v2 covariantly damped Maxwell--Debye model has the verified stage-2 monotone
energy identity, but the stage-3 interface calculation shows that it is not a
perfectly matched layer.  In an \(x\)-layer with \(\rho_x=\rho>0,\rho_y=0\),
\[
Y_{v2}^2-Y_0^2
=-\frac{\rho}{\mu^2}\left[
\frac{\mu\chi\tau}{(1+\tau s)(1+\tau(s+\rho))}
+\frac{k_y^2}{s^2(s+\rho)}
\right],
\]
so the v2 reflection coefficient is not identically zero.

Therefore a repaired model must keep the physical Debye law as a function of the
Laplace variable \(s\), not \(s+\rho\), and must implement damping through
coordinate stretching or an equivalent split/ADE system.

## Candidate 1: classical stretched-coordinate Maxwell--Debye PML

Let
\[
\varepsilon_D(s)=\epsilon_0\epsilon_\infty+\frac{\chi}{1+\tau s},
\qquad
S_i(s)=1+\frac{\sigma_i}{s},\quad i=x,y.
\]
In the physical region \(\sigma_x=\sigma_y=0\).  In the PML the coefficients are
nonnegative and are first analyzed as piecewise constant near each planar
interface.

The Laplace-domain repaired model is
\[
\boxed{
s\varepsilon_D(s)\widehat E
=S_x^{-1}\partial_x\widehat H_y
-S_y^{-1}\partial_y\widehat H_x,}
\]
\[
\boxed{
\mu s\widehat H_x=-S_y^{-1}\partial_y\widehat E,\qquad
\mu s\widehat H_y=S_x^{-1}\partial_x\widehat E,}
\]
\[
\boxed{(1+\tau s)\widehat P=\chi\widehat E.}
\]
Equivalently, the Debye law is not damped:
\[
P+\tau P_t=\chi E.
\]

### Perfect matching

At an \(x\)-interface, \(S_y=1\).  With tangential Fourier number \(k_y\),
the physical normal symbol satisfies
\[
\nu_0^2=k_y^2+\mu s^2\varepsilon_D(s),\qquad
Y_0=\frac{\nu_0}{\mu s}.
\]
In the PML,
\[
s\varepsilon_D E=S_x^{-1}\nu H_y-ik_yH_x,\qquad
\mu sH_x=-ik_yE,\qquad
\mu sH_y=S_x^{-1}\nu E.
\]
The dispersion relation gives
\[
\left(S_x^{-1}\nu\right)^2=k_y^2+\mu s^2\varepsilon_D(s),
\]
hence \(\nu=S_x\nu_0\) and
\[
Y_+=\frac{S_x^{-1}\nu}{\mu s}=\frac{\nu_0}{\mu s}=Y_0.
\]
Thus the planar-interface reflection coefficient is \(R=0\) for every
\((s,k_y)\) in the Laplace half-plane.  The same argument applies to a
\(y\)-interface with \(x,y\) interchanged.

### Time-domain ADE realization

Define the causal operator
\[
\mathcal A_i=S_i^{-1}=\frac{s}{s+\sigma_i}
\]
in the Laplace domain.  Equivalently,
\[
\mathcal A_i f=f+\psi_i,\qquad
(\partial_t+\sigma_i)\psi_i=-\sigma_i f.
\]
Then a time-domain unsplit ADE form is
\[
\epsilon_0\epsilon_\infty E_t+P_t
=\partial_xH_y-\partial_yH_x
+\psi_{E,x}-\psi_{E,y},
\]
\[
\mu H_{x,t}=-\partial_yE-\psi_{H_x,y},\qquad
\mu H_{y,t}=\partial_xE+\psi_{H_y,x},
\]
\[
P+\tau P_t=\chi E,
\]
with
\[
(\partial_t+\sigma_x)\psi_{E,x}=-\sigma_x\partial_xH_y,\qquad
(\partial_t+\sigma_y)\psi_{E,y}=-\sigma_y\partial_yH_x,
\]
\[
(\partial_t+\sigma_y)\psi_{H_x,y}=-\sigma_y\partial_yE,\qquad
(\partial_t+\sigma_x)\psi_{H_y,x}=-\sigma_x\partial_xE.
\]
Interface conditions are continuity of the physical tangential traces.  For an
\(x\)-interface these are \(E\) and \(H_y\).  The auxiliary variables vanish in the
physical region and are initialized consistently with the causal convolution.

### Naive energy calculation

The natural physical Debye energy is
\[
\mathcal E_{\rm phys}
=\frac12\int_\Omega
\left(\epsilon_0\epsilon_\infty E^2+\mu H_x^2+\mu H_y^2+\chi^{-1}P^2\right)\,dxdy.
\]
It is positive because
\(\epsilon_0,\epsilon_\infty,\mu,\chi>0\).  Using
\[
E P_t=\frac{1}{2\chi}\partial_t(P^2)+\frac{\tau}{\chi}P_t^2
\]
and the PEC boundary condition \(E=0\) on the outer boundary gives
\[
\frac{d}{dt}\mathcal E_{\rm phys}
=-\int_\Omega\frac{\tau}{\chi}P_t^2\,dxdy
+\int_\Omega
\left[
E(\psi_{E,x}-\psi_{E,y})
-H_x\psi_{H_x,y}
+H_y\psi_{H_y,x}
\right]\,dxdy .
\]
The Maxwell principal part contributes only the boundary flux
\[
\int_{\partial\Omega}E(H_y n_x-H_x n_y)\,ds,
\]
which vanishes under PEC at the outer boundary and cancels by transmission at
internal material/PML interfaces when the tangential traces are continuous.

The remaining auxiliary terms are not sign-definite in this naive energy.
Therefore the positive physical Debye energy alone is not a monotone energy for
the exact stretched-coordinate PML.

### Classification

This candidate is the formula-level perfect-matching repair.  A local monotone
energy for the full 2D Maxwell--Debye ADE system is not certified here.  The
calculation above identifies the exact terms that a Baffet-type augmented energy
would have to absorb:
\[
E\psi_{E,x},\quad E\psi_{E,y},\quad
H_x\psi_{H_x,y},\quad H_y\psi_{H_y,x}.
\]
The literature record supports that such augmented energies are non-naive and
that constant-coefficient damping is the natural first scope for a sharp identity.

### Reduced normal-incidence 1D energy identity

There is one important positive result for the exact stretched-coordinate model.
In the \(x\)-layer normal-incidence block \(k_y=0\), the standard stretch gives
\[
(\partial_t+\rho)(\epsilon_0\epsilon_\infty E+P)=\partial_xH_y,
\qquad
\mu(\partial_t+\rho)H_y=\partial_xE,
\]
\[
P+\tau P_t=\chi E.
\]
This is exactly the \(k_y=0\) restriction of the perfectly matched stretched
model, not the v2 model, because the Debye law still uses \(\partial_t\) rather
than \(\partial_t+\rho\).

Multiply the first equation by \(E\), the second by \(H_y\), and use
\[
E=\frac{P+\tau P_t}{\chi}.
\]
Then
\[
E P_t=\frac{1}{2\chi}\partial_t(P^2)+\frac{\tau}{\chi}P_t^2,
\]
and
\[
\rho E P
=\frac{\rho}{\chi}P^2+\frac{\rho\tau}{2\chi}\partial_t(P^2).
\]
After integrating by parts, the principal terms give only the boundary flux
\(\int_{\partial I}EH_y n_x\,ds\).  Hence
\[
\boxed{
\frac{d}{dt}\mathcal E_{1d,sc}
=-\int_I\left(
\rho\epsilon_0\epsilon_\infty E^2+\mu\rho H_y^2
+\frac{\rho}{\chi}P^2+\frac{\tau}{\chi}P_t^2
\right)\,dx
+\int_{\partial I}EH_y n_x\,ds,}
\]
where
\[
\boxed{
\mathcal E_{1d,sc}
=\frac12\int_I\left(
\epsilon_0\epsilon_\infty E^2+\mu H_y^2
+\frac{1+\rho\tau}{\chi}P^2
\right)\,dx.}
\]
This energy is positive for \(\rho,\tau,\chi>0\), and it is dissipative under
PEC or otherwise nonpositive boundary flux.  It explains why the v2 idea is
close to a useful construction in normal incidence, but it does not solve the
full 2D oblique problem: as soon as \(k_y\ne0\), the exact stretched model
contains the ADE memory couplings displayed above.

## Candidate 2: generalized CFS/ADE stretched-coordinate PML

Let
\[
S_i(s)=\kappa_i+\frac{\sigma_i}{s+\alpha_i},
\qquad
\kappa_i\ge1,\quad \sigma_i\ge0,\quad \alpha_i\ge0.
\]
The repaired Laplace-domain equations are the same as Candidate 1, with these
\(S_i\).  In particular the Debye law remains
\[
(1+\tau s)\widehat P=\chi\widehat E.
\]

For a planar \(x\)-interface with \(S_y=1\), the same calculation gives
\[
\nu=S_x\nu_0,\qquad Y_+=Y_0,
\]
so the continuous model is perfectly matched whenever the stretch is applied to
the spatial derivatives and the physical material law is left unchanged.

If \(S_i^{-1}\) is rational with poles in \(\Re s<0\), it can be implemented by
ADE variables.  The CFS shift \(\alpha_i>0\) is a standard way to improve
low-frequency/evanescent and late-time behavior, but a monotone time-domain
energy requires an explicit positive realization of the memory kernel.  No such
positive memory theorem is claimed here for the full 2D Maxwell--Debye system.

Classification: perfectly matched at the continuous planar-interface level;
recommended if long-time CFS behavior is needed; energy status is boundedness or
passive-memory proof pending, not a completed monotone identity.

## Candidate 3: MPML-type extra damping

An MPML-type repair adds damping in more than the normal coordinate direction.
For example, in an \(x\)-layer one may replace a scalar stretch by a multiaxial
stretch depending also on tangential damping parameters.  This is useful for
removing long-time instabilities or Jordan-block behavior in some systems.

However, if the tangential stretch is nontrivial at the physical/PML interface,
the planar admittance generally changes.  The MPML literature inspected for this
run explicitly treats MPML as a stability-oriented absorbing layer and records
that exact perfect matching may be lost in multiaxial variants.

Classification: absorbing/stability repair, not the primary exact-matching
repair for the present Maxwell--Debye interface theorem.

## Complete dissipative identity that is currently verified

The only complete positive monotone identity verified in the existing Iteris
memory is for the v2 covariantly damped absorbing layer:
\[
\epsilon_0\epsilon_\infty D_\rho E
=\partial_xH_y-\partial_yH_x-D_\rho P,
\]
\[
\mu(\partial_t+\rho_y)H_x=-\partial_yE,\qquad
\mu(\partial_t+\rho_x)H_y=\partial_xE,
\]
\[
P+\tau D_\rho P=\chi E,\qquad D_\rho=\partial_t+\rho_x+\rho_y.
\]
Its energy is
\[
\mathcal E_\rho(t)=\frac12\int_\Omega
\left(\epsilon_0\epsilon_\infty E^2+\mu H_x^2+\mu H_y^2+\chi^{-1}P^2\right)\,dxdy
\]
and the verified identity is
\[
\frac{d}{dt}\mathcal E_\rho(t)
=-\int_\Omega\left(
\epsilon_0\epsilon_\infty\rho E^2
+\mu\rho_yH_x^2
+\mu\rho_xH_y^2
+\frac{\rho}{\chi}P^2
+\frac{\tau}{\chi}|D_\rho P|^2
\right)\,dxdy.
\]
This identity is genuinely dissipative, but the model is not perfectly matched.
It should therefore be described as a stable absorbing-layer model, not as a
standard PML.

## Formula-level obstruction to strict decay on the whole domain

Even for a perfectly matched repair, strict decay of a total energy controlling
all fields on the whole computational domain cannot hold without a nullspace.
Assume a physical subregion where \(\sigma_x=\sigma_y=0\) and choose
\[
E=0,\qquad P=0,\qquad H_x=\partial_x\phi,\qquad H_y=\partial_y\phi,
\]
with \(\phi\) smooth and compactly supported inside that undamped physical
subregion.  Then
\[
\partial_xH_y-\partial_yH_x=0,\qquad
\partial_yE=\partial_xE=0,
\]
and all PML auxiliary variables initialized at zero remain zero for at least this
exact stationary solution.  The magnetic energy is positive if \(\nabla\phi\ne0\),
but every damping term in the PML vanishes.

Therefore no theorem can honestly state that the total energy is strictly
decreasing for every nonzero state on the whole computational domain.  The sharp
possible statement is a dissipative identity or inequality whose nullspace
contains undamped physical-region stationary/curl-free magnetic modes and, more
generally, states not seen by the layer damping.

# Stage-3 proof: Baffet-type 2D energy for a matched Maxwell-Debye PML

Problem id: `2d_maxwell_pml_energy_functional_exploration`

Task: `task-stage3-final-report`

## Purpose

The previous stage-3 artifact proves that the standard stretched-coordinate
Maxwell-Debye PML is perfectly matched, but only gives a monotone energy in the
one-dimensional normal-incidence block.  This artifact records a full two
dimensional constant-coefficient Baffet-type formulation for the same stretched
coordinate model.  The formulation uses a time primitive of the electric field
and a time primitive of the Debye polarization, which is exactly the type of
augmented/time-integrated variable used in Baffet-type PML energy arguments.

## Assumptions and notation

Let
\[
e=\epsilon_0\epsilon_\infty>0,\quad \mu>0,\quad \chi>0,\quad \tau>0.
\]
In the Laplace domain,
\[
\varepsilon_D(s)=e+\frac{\chi}{1+\tau s}.
\]
On one constant-coefficient PML block let
\[
\sigma_x,\sigma_y\ge 0,\qquad
a=\sigma_x+\sigma_y,\qquad b=\sigma_x\sigma_y,
\]
and assume \(a>0\) for the PML block.  The undamped physical block \(a=b=0\)
uses the ordinary Maxwell-Debye energy and is coupled by the usual transmission
flux.  Define
\[
\Gamma_1=\begin{pmatrix}\sigma_x&0\\0&\sigma_y\end{pmatrix},\qquad
\Gamma_2=\begin{pmatrix}\sigma_y-\sigma_x&0\\0&\sigma_x-\sigma_y\end{pmatrix}.
\]
For a vector \(v\), write \(|v|_M^2=v\cdot Mv\).

Let \(u\) be the time primitive of the electric field:
\[
E=u_t.
\]
Let \(q\) be the time primitive of the Debye polarization:
\[
q_t=P.
\]
The Debye law is written in compatible primitive form
\[
\tau P_t+P=\chi u_t,\qquad q+\tau P=\chi u.
\]
The second relation is preserved by the first two equations if it is true at
initial time.

## Baffet-type matched PML system

Introduce the Baffet auxiliary vector \(\phi=(\phi_x,\phi_y)\) and
\[
\lambda=\nabla u+\phi.
\]
The constant-coefficient two-dimensional repaired model is
\[
\boxed{
\mu\{e(u_{tt}+a u_t+b u)+P_t+aP+bq\}-\nabla\cdot\lambda=0,}
\tag{1}
\]
\[
\boxed{\phi_t+\Gamma_1\phi=\Gamma_2\nabla u,}
\tag{2}
\]
\[
\boxed{\tau P_t+P=\chi u_t,\qquad q_t=P,\qquad q+\tau P=\chi u.}
\tag{3}
\]
Outer boundary conditions are taken so that the boundary flux
\[
\int_{\partial\Omega}(u_t+au)\lambda\cdot n\,ds
\]
is zero or nonpositive.  For a PEC outer boundary, the compatible primitive
condition is \(u=0\), hence \(u_t=E=0\), on that boundary.  On piecewise
constant internal interfaces, the usual transmission conditions are continuity
of \(u\) and \(\lambda\cdot n\), so the flux cancels pairwise.

## Equivalence with the stretched-coordinate Maxwell-Debye PML

For constant coefficients, Laplace transforming (2) gives
\[
\widehat\phi_x=\frac{\sigma_y-\sigma_x}{s+\sigma_x}\partial_x\widehat u,
\qquad
\widehat\phi_y=\frac{\sigma_x-\sigma_y}{s+\sigma_y}\partial_y\widehat u.
\]
Thus
\[
\widehat\lambda_x
=\frac{s+\sigma_y}{s+\sigma_x}\partial_x\widehat u
=\frac{S_y}{S_x}\partial_x\widehat u,\qquad
\widehat\lambda_y
=\frac{s+\sigma_x}{s+\sigma_y}\partial_y\widehat u
=\frac{S_x}{S_y}\partial_y\widehat u,
\]
where
\[
S_i(s)=1+\frac{\sigma_i}{s}=\frac{s+\sigma_i}{s}.
\]
The Debye compatibility gives
\[
\widehat P=\frac{\chi s}{1+\tau s}\widehat u,\qquad
\widehat q=\frac{1}{s}\widehat P.
\]
Therefore
\[
e(s^2+as+b)\widehat u+s\widehat P+a\widehat P+b\widehat q
=\left(e+\frac{\chi}{1+\tau s}\right)(s^2+as+b)\widehat u
=\varepsilon_D(s)s^2S_xS_y\widehat u.
\]
Equation (1) becomes
\[
\mu\varepsilon_D(s)s^2S_xS_y\widehat u
=\nabla\cdot\widehat\lambda.
\]
Dividing by \(S_xS_y\) gives
\[
\mu\varepsilon_D(s)s^2\widehat u
=S_x^{-1}\partial_x(S_x^{-1}\partial_x\widehat u)
+S_y^{-1}\partial_y(S_y^{-1}\partial_y\widehat u).
\]
Since \(\widehat E=s\widehat u\), this is exactly the second-order equation
obtained by eliminating \(H_x,H_y\) from the standard stretched-coordinate
Maxwell-Debye PML while keeping
\[
(1+\tau s)\widehat P=\chi \widehat E.
\]
Consequently this Baffet-type time-domain system has the same planar-interface
perfect matching as the standard stretched-coordinate PML: at an \(x\)-interface
with \(S_y=1\), the normal symbol satisfies \(\nu=S_x\nu_0\) and the tangential
Maxwell admittance is unchanged.

## Energy functional

Define
\[
\alpha=1+2a\tau,\qquad
\beta=a+b\tau,\qquad
\gamma=a^2+b(1+a\tau).
\]
The Baffet-Debye energy is
\[
\boxed{
\begin{aligned}
\mathcal E_{BD}
=\frac12\int_\Omega \{&
\mu e(u_t+a u)^2+|\lambda|^2
+|\phi|_{a^{-1}\Gamma_1}^2+\mu e\,b u^2\\
&+\frac{\mu}{\chi}\left(\alpha P^2+2\beta Pq+\gamma q^2\right)
\}\,dxdy .
\end{aligned}}
\tag{4}
\]
The \(P,q\) block is positive definite whenever \(a>0\).  Indeed
\[
\alpha>0,\qquad
\alpha\gamma-\beta^2
=b+ab\tau+2a^3\tau+b(2a^2-b)\tau^2>0,
\]
because \(a=\sigma_x+\sigma_y>0\), \(b=\sigma_x\sigma_y\ge0\), \(\tau>0\), and
\(2a^2-b\ge0\).  Thus (4) is nonnegative, and it is coercive on the PML block
modulo the usual zero modes of the primitive variables and boundary conditions.

## Energy identity

Test (1) with \(u_t+a u\).  The nondispersive part gives the usual Baffet
calculation:
\[
\frac12\frac{d}{dt}\int_\Omega
\mu e\{(u_t+a u)^2+b u^2\}\,dxdy
+\int_\Omega \mu e\,ab u^2\,dxdy
=\int_\Omega (u_t+a u)\nabla\cdot\lambda\,dxdy
-\mu\int_\Omega (P_t+aP+bq)(u_t+a u)\,dxdy .
\tag{5}
\]
The boundary part of the first term is the flux stated above, and the interior
part is handled by the same Baffet multiplier used for \(\lambda\).  Specifically,
from
\[
\lambda_t+\Gamma_1\lambda=\nabla u_t+\widetilde\Gamma_2\nabla u,\qquad
\widetilde\Gamma_2=\Gamma_2+\Gamma_1
=\begin{pmatrix}\sigma_y&0\\0&\sigma_x\end{pmatrix},
\]
and the multiplier
\[
g=(I+a^{-1}\Gamma_1)\lambda-a^{-1}\Gamma_1\nabla u,
\]
one obtains
\[
\begin{aligned}
&\frac12\frac{d}{dt}\int_\Omega
\left(|\lambda|^2+|\phi|_{a^{-1}\Gamma_1}^2\right)\,dxdy\\
&\quad+\int_\Omega
\left(|\lambda|^2_{\Gamma_1(I+a^{-1}\Gamma_1)}
+\frac{b}{a}|\nabla u|^2\right)\,dxdy
=\int_\Omega \nabla(u_t+a u)\cdot\lambda\,dxdy .
\end{aligned}
\tag{6}
\]
This is the two-dimensional Baffet identity; it uses
\(\Gamma_1\widetilde\Gamma_2=bI\) and
\(a^{-1}\Gamma_1(\Gamma_1+\widetilde\Gamma_2)+\widetilde\Gamma_2=aI\).

It remains to compute the Debye primitive contribution.  Using
\[
u_t+a u
=\frac{\tau P_t+(1+a\tau)P+a q}{\chi},
\]
we have
\[
\begin{aligned}
&(P_t+aP+bq)(u_t+a u)\\
&=\frac1\chi\Big[
\frac12\frac{d}{dt}
\left(\alpha P^2+2\beta Pq+\gamma q^2\right)
+\tau P_t^2+\tau(a^2-b)P^2+abq^2
\Big].
\end{aligned}
\tag{7}
\]
Here \(q_t=P\), and the constants \(\alpha,\beta,\gamma\) are exactly those in
(4).

Adding (5), (6), and (7) gives the full identity
\[
\boxed{
\frac{d}{dt}\mathcal E_{BD}(t)
=-\mathcal D_{BD}(t)
+\int_{\partial\Omega}(u_t+a u)\lambda\cdot n\,ds,}
\tag{8}
\]
where
\[
\boxed{
\begin{aligned}
\mathcal D_{BD}
=\int_\Omega \{&
|\lambda|^2_{\Gamma_1(I+a^{-1}\Gamma_1)}
+\frac{b}{a}|\nabla u|^2+\mu e\,ab u^2\\
&+\frac{\mu}{\chi}\left[
\tau P_t^2+\tau(a^2-b)P^2+abq^2
\right]\}\,dxdy .
\end{aligned}}
\tag{9}
\]
All displayed terms in \(\mathcal D_{BD}\) are nonnegative for
\(\sigma_x,\sigma_y\ge0\), \(a>0\), and positive material parameters.  Under PEC
or canceling transmission flux, (8) gives
\[
\mathcal E_{BD}(t)+\int_0^t\mathcal D_{BD}(r)\,dr\le \mathcal E_{BD}(0).
\]

## Classification and nullspace

This is a full two-dimensional constant-coefficient dissipative identity for an
exact stretched-coordinate Maxwell-Debye PML, written in Baffet-type
time-integrated variables.  It is non-increasing, not strictly decreasing on the
whole computational domain.  The nullspace contains the already identified
undamped physical-region stationary magnetic modes; in the PML block, the
dissipation also leaves the standard primitive-variable gauge modes unless fixed
by boundary/transmission compatibility.  Thus the sharp statement is
non-increase plus a characterized nullspace/no-abnormal-growth estimate, not
strict decay of every nonzero whole-domain state.

For spatially varying damping profiles, this artifact does not claim an energy
identity.  As in the Baffet reference, the verified scope is constant
coefficients, and piecewise constant layers are handled blockwise with
transmission flux cancellation.

stretched-coordinate PML 的能量 theorem。常系数块中使用 \(u_t=E,q_t=P\)，证明

\frac{d}{dt}\mathcal E_{BD}(t)
=-\mathcal D_{BD}(t)
+\int_{\partial\Omega}(u_t+a u)\lambda\cdot n\,ds,
\qquad \mathcal D_{BD}\ge0.
\]

## Verified Obstruction From The Old Model

The old alpha \(=1\) source model uses
\[
E,\ H_x,\ H_y,\ P,\ P_{z,1},\ P_{z,2},\ Q_x,\ Q_y .
\]
With
\[
a_x=\frac{\sigma_y-\sigma_x}{\epsilon_0},\qquad
a_y=\frac{\sigma_x-\sigma_y}{\epsilon_0},
\]
the shifted magnetic variables
\[
M_x=Q_x-\mu a_xH_x,\qquad M_y=Q_y-\mu a_yH_y
\]
satisfy
\[
M_{x,t}=a_x\partial_yE-\frac{\sigma_y}{\epsilon_0}M_x,\qquad
M_{y,t}=-a_y\partial_xE-\frac{\sigma_x}{\epsilon_0}M_y .
\]

In an \(x\)-edge PML with constant \(\sigma_x=s>0,\sigma_y=0\), the ansatz
\[
E=P=P_{z,1}=P_{z,2}=H_y=Q_y=0
\]
with spatially constant \(H_x,Q_x\) gives
\[
M_x=Q_x+\mu\frac{s}{\epsilon_0}H_x=\text{constant}
\]
and therefore
\[
H_x(t)=H_x(0)+\frac{M_x(0)}{\mu}t,\qquad
Q_x(t)=Q_x(0)-\frac{s}{\epsilon_0}M_x(0)t .
\]
The obstruction is the undamped shifted magnetic auxiliary in the edge
direction.  Since this exact solution has \(P=0\), changing only the Debye or
fractional polarization law cannot remove it.

## Repair 1: Compatibility Restriction

For the old equations, the minimal compatibility condition that kills the
verified constant edge mode is
\[
Q_x(0)+\mu\frac{\sigma_x}{\epsilon_0}H_x(0)=0
\quad\text{on an \(x\)-edge zero-transverse mode,}
\]
and symmetrically
\[
Q_y(0)+\mu\frac{\sigma_y}{\epsilon_0}H_y(0)=0
\quad\text{on a \(y\)-edge zero-transverse mode.}
\]
This is physically meaningful if the \(Q_i\) are not independent data but
history variables generated by a PML construction.

Candidate energy:
\[
\mathcal E_0=\frac12\int_\Omega
\left(\epsilon_0\epsilon_\infty E^2+\mu H_x^2+\mu H_y^2
+\chi^{-1}P^2+P_{z,1}^2+P_{z,2}^2+Q_x^2+Q_y^2\right)\,dxdy .
\]
It is positive, and the previous verified result gives
\[
\mathcal E_0'(t)\le C_G\mathcal E_0(t).
\]

Classification: useful but partial.  In a genuine 2D \(x\)-edge,
\[
M_{x,t}=-\frac{\sigma_x}{\epsilon_0}\partial_yE,
\]
so pointwise \(M_x=0\) is not invariant for arbitrary two-dimensional data.
This route removes the verified zero-transverse free mode but does not produce
a full 2D monotone energy for the old model.

## Repair 2: Shifted-Variable MPML Damping

Keep the old shifted variables but add edge-positive damping
\(\eta_x,\eta_y\ge0\):
\[
Q_{x,t}=-(b_x+\eta_x)Q_x+\mu(b_x+\eta_x)a_xH_x,
\]
\[
Q_{y,t}=-(b_y+\eta_y)Q_y+\mu(b_y+\eta_y)a_yH_y,
\]
where \(b_i=\sigma_i/\epsilon_0\).  Equivalently,
\[
M_{x,t}=a_x\partial_yE-(b_y+\eta_x)M_x,\qquad
M_{y,t}=-a_y\partial_xE-(b_x+\eta_y)M_y .
\]

For the old \(x\)-edge free subsystem this becomes
\[
H_{x,t}=\frac{M_x}{\mu},\qquad M_{x,t}=-\eta_xM_x .
\]
If \(\eta_x>0\), then
\[
\mathcal E_{x,\eta}
=\frac{\mu}{2}\left|H_x+\frac{M_x}{\mu\eta_x}\right|^2
+\frac{c_x}{2}|M_x|^2,\qquad c_x>0,
\]
is positive and satisfies
\[
\frac{d}{dt}\mathcal E_{x,\eta}=-c_x\eta_x|M_x|^2\le0 .
\]

Classification: monotone for the isolated edge free mode and a plausible
MPML/CFS repair of the old Jordan block.  In full 2D it still leaves
\(M_x\partial_yE\) and \(M_y\partial_xE\) couplings, so the completed theorem
would need derivative, nonlocal, or Baffet-type structure.

## Selected Model: Covariantly Damped Maxwell-Debye Layer

The strongest verified constructive result is a modified alpha \(=1\)
Maxwell-Debye absorbing-layer model.  Let
\[
\rho_x,\rho_y\in L^\infty(\Omega),\qquad \rho_x,\rho_y\ge0,\qquad
\rho=\rho_x+\rho_y,\qquad D_\rho=\partial_t+\rho .
\]
The profiles vanish in the physical region and are positive in the absorbing
layer.

The model is
\[
\boxed{
\begin{aligned}
\epsilon_0\epsilon_\infty D_\rho E
&=\partial_xH_y-\partial_yH_x-D_\rho P,\\
\mu(\partial_t+\rho_y)H_x&=-\partial_yE,\\
\mu(\partial_t+\rho_x)H_y&=\partial_xE,\\
P+\tau D_\rho P&=\chi E,
\end{aligned}}
\]
with PEC boundary condition \(E=0\) on \(\partial\Omega\).

This model removes the independent \(P_{z,i},Q_i\) variables.  The old edge
auxiliary mode is therefore absent.  The important design choice is applying
the same covariant derivative \(D_\rho\) to the Debye law; this changes the old
sign-indefinite \(EP\) damping term into positive polarization dissipation.

## Energy Functional

Use
\[
\boxed{
\mathcal E_\rho(t)=\frac12\int_\Omega
\left(\epsilon_0\epsilon_\infty E^2+\mu H_x^2+\mu H_y^2+\chi^{-1}P^2\right)
\,dxdy .}
\]
This energy is positive definite because
\(\epsilon_0,\epsilon_\infty,\mu,\chi>0\).

## Energy Identity

Multiplying the equations by \(E,H_x,H_y\), integrating, and using PEC gives
the usual Maxwell cancellation:
\[
\int_\Omega(E\partial_xH_y-E\partial_yH_x-H_x\partial_yE+H_y\partial_xE)\,dxdy=0 .
\]
The covariant Debye law gives
\[
E\,D_\rho P
=\frac{1}{2\chi}\partial_t(P^2)
+\frac{\rho}{\chi}P^2
+\frac{\tau}{\chi}|D_\rho P|^2 .
\]
Therefore
\[
\boxed{
\frac{d}{dt}\mathcal E_\rho(t)
=-\int_\Omega\left(
\epsilon_0\epsilon_\infty\rho E^2
+\mu\rho_yH_x^2
+\mu\rho_xH_y^2
+\frac{\rho}{\chi}P^2
+\frac{\tau}{\chi}|D_\rho P|^2
\right)\,dxdy\le0 .}
\]
Thus
\[
\boxed{\mathcal E_\rho(t)\le \mathcal E_\rho(0)\quad\text{for all }t\ge0.}
\]

Classification: monotone decreasing, dissipative, and uniformly bounded in
long time.  It is a repaired absorbing-layer model, not a proof that the old
eight-variable unsplit source PML is monotone.

1. Exact perfect matching for the selected covariantly damped model is not
proved here.  The verified result is stability and layer dissipation.
2. The shifted MPML repair needs a full 2D derivative or nonlocal energy to
control \(M_x\partial_yE\) and \(M_y\partial_xE\).
3. The compatibility route should be sharpened by Fourier analysis of the
transverse zero-mode projection and by a boundary-compatible definition of the

4. The fractional case \(0<\alpha<1\) can be added later by replacing the

it cannot remove the old edge obstruction by itself because that obstruction

E,\ H_x,\ H_y,\ P,\ P_{z,1},\ P_{z,2},\ Q_x,\ Q_y

P+\tau^\alpha\partial_t^\alpha P=\chi E,\qquad

This report analyzes \(\alpha=1\).  The fractional case \(0<\alpha<1\) is postponed

## Model used

For \(\alpha=1\), the equations used are exactly
\[
\begin{aligned}
\epsilon_0\epsilon_\infty E_t
&= \partial_xH_y-\partial_yH_x
   -\epsilon_\infty(\sigma_x+\sigma_y)E
   -P_t-\frac{\sigma_x+\sigma_y}{\epsilon_0}P
   +P_{z,1}+P_{z,2},\\
\mu H_{x,t}
&= -\partial_yE-\mu\frac{\sigma_y-\sigma_x}{\epsilon_0}H_x+Q_x,\\
\mu H_{y,t}
&= \partial_xE-\mu\frac{\sigma_x-\sigma_y}{\epsilon_0}H_y+Q_y,\\
P+\tau P_t&=\chi E,\\
P_{z,1,t}&=-\frac{\epsilon_\infty}{\epsilon_0}\sigma_x\sigma_y E,\\
P_{z,2,t}&=-\frac{\sigma_x\sigma_y}{\epsilon_0^2}P,\\
Q_{x,t}&=-\frac{\sigma_x}{\epsilon_0}Q_x
  +\frac{\mu\sigma_x(\sigma_y-\sigma_x)}{\epsilon_0^2}H_x,\\
Q_{y,t}&=-\frac{\sigma_y}{\epsilon_0}Q_y
  +\frac{\mu\sigma_y(\sigma_x-\sigma_y)}{\epsilon_0^2}H_y .
\end{aligned}
\]
The boundary assumption is PEC:
\[
E=0\quad\text{on }\partial\Omega .
\]
The absorption assumptions for the Gronwall estimate are
\[
\sigma_x,\sigma_y\in L^\infty(\Omega),\qquad \sigma_x,\sigma_y\ge0,
\]
with time-independent coefficients.  This includes constant, separated-variable, and
general spatially variable profiles.

## Verified alpha=1 balance

The electromagnetic energy is
\[
\mathcal E_{\rm em}
=\frac12\int_\Omega
\left(\epsilon_0\epsilon_\infty E^2+\mu H_x^2+\mu H_y^2\right)\,dxdy .
\]
PEC makes the Maxwell principal boundary flux
\[
\int_{\partial\Omega}E(H_y n_x-H_x n_y)\,ds
\]
vanish.  Using \(P+\tau P_t=\chi E\),
\[
E P_t=\frac{1}{2\chi}\frac{d}{dt}\|P\|_2^2
+\frac{\tau}{\chi}\|P_t\|_2^2 .
\]
Thus
\[
\mathcal E_{\rm em+P}
=\mathcal E_{\rm em}+\frac1{2\chi}\|P\|_2^2
\]
is positive and satisfies
\[
\begin{aligned}
\frac{d}{dt}\mathcal E_{\rm em+P}
=\int_\Omega\Big[
&-\epsilon_\infty(\sigma_x+\sigma_y)E^2
-\frac{\tau}{\chi}P_t^2
-\frac{\sigma_x+\sigma_y}{\epsilon_0}EP
+E(P_{z,1}+P_{z,2})\\
&-\frac{\mu}{\epsilon_0}(\sigma_y-\sigma_x)H_x^2
-\frac{\mu}{\epsilon_0}(\sigma_x-\sigma_y)H_y^2
+H_xQ_x+H_yQ_y
\Big]\,dxdy .
\end{aligned}
\]

With
\[
a_x=\frac{\sigma_y-\sigma_x}{\epsilon_0},\quad
a_y=\frac{\sigma_x-\sigma_y}{\epsilon_0},\quad
b_x=\frac{\sigma_x}{\epsilon_0},\quad
b_y=\frac{\sigma_y}{\epsilon_0},
\]
and shifted variables
\[
M_x=Q_x-\mu a_xH_x,\qquad M_y=Q_y-\mu a_yH_y,
\]
one has
\[
\mu H_{x,t}=-\partial_yE+M_x,\quad
\mu H_{y,t}=\partial_xE+M_y,
\]
\[
M_{x,t}=a_x\partial_yE-b_yM_x,\qquad
M_{y,t}=-a_y\partial_xE-b_xM_y .
\]
Substitution cancels the sign-indefinite magnetic squares and leaves
\[
\begin{aligned}
\frac{d}{dt}\mathcal E_{\rm em+P}
=\int_\Omega\Big[
&-\epsilon_\infty(\sigma_x+\sigma_y)E^2
-\frac{\tau}{\chi}P_t^2
-\frac{\sigma_x+\sigma_y}{\epsilon_0}EP
+E(P_{z,1}+P_{z,2})\\
&+H_xM_x+H_yM_y
\Big]\,dxdy .
\end{aligned}
\]

## Positive Gronwall energy

The positive augmented energy proved here is
\[
\mathcal E_0(t)
=\frac12\int_\Omega
\left(\epsilon_0\epsilon_\infty E^2+\mu H_x^2+\mu H_y^2
+\chi^{-1}P^2+P_{z,1}^2+P_{z,2}^2+Q_x^2+Q_y^2\right)\,dxdy .
\]
Adding the \(L^2\) derivatives of \(P_{z,1},P_{z,2},Q_x,Q_y\) to the verified
balance and applying Young's inequality gives
\[
\boxed{\frac{d}{dt}\mathcal E_0(t)\le C_G\mathcal E_0(t)}
\]
with \(C_G<\infty\) depending only on the material constants and the \(L^\infty\)
sizes of
\[
\sigma_x,\ \sigma_y,\ \sigma_x\sigma_y,\ 
\sigma_x(\sigma_y-\sigma_x),\ 
\sigma_y(\sigma_x-\sigma_y).
\]
Therefore
\[
\boxed{\mathcal E_0(t)\le e^{C_Gt}\mathcal E_0(0).}
\]
This is a Gronwall-type estimate.  It is not monotone and not uniform in long time.

The possible-growth terms are exactly
\[
EP,\quad EP_{z,1},\quad EP_{z,2},\quad PP_{z,2},\quad H_xQ_x,\quad H_yQ_y,
\]
together with the magnetic sign-indefinite square terms before the shift.  In shifted
variables the magnetic issue becomes \(H_xM_x+H_yM_y\).  Adding plain
\(\|M_x\|_2^2+\|M_y\|_2^2\) is not a closed local \(L^2\) monotone fix because its
derivative contains \(M_x\partial_yE\) and \(M_y\partial_xE\).

## Case split

### No PML

If \(\sigma_x=\sigma_y=0\) and the PML auxiliaries are initially zero, then
\[
P_{z,1}=P_{z,2}=Q_x=Q_y=0
\]
for all time, and
\[
\frac{d}{dt}\mathcal E_{\rm em+P}
=-\frac{\tau}{\chi}\|P_t\|_2^2\le0 .
\]
So the no-PML Debye-Maxwell subsystem has a monotone positive alpha \(=1\) energy
under the natural auxiliary-zero compatibility condition.

### Edge PML

For constant \(\sigma_x=s>0,\sigma_y=0\), set
\[
E=P=P_{z,1}=P_{z,2}=H_y=Q_y=0
\]
and take \(H_x,Q_x\) spatially constant.  With \(b=s/\epsilon_0\),
\[
H_{x,t}=bH_x+\frac1\mu Q_x,\qquad
Q_{x,t}=-bQ_x-\mu b^2H_x .
\]
The shifted quantity
\[
M_x=Q_x+\mu bH_x
\]
is constant, hence
\[
H_x(t)=H_x(0)+\frac{M_x(0)}{\mu}t,\qquad
Q_x(t)=Q_x(0)-bM_x(0)t .
\]
If \(M_x(0)\ne0\), \(H_x,Q_x\) grow linearly while \(E=0\) satisfies PEC.

The case \(\sigma_x=0,\sigma_y=s>0\) has the symmetric construction with \(H_y,Q_y\)
and constant \(M_y=Q_y+\mu bH_y\).

Therefore the source model as stated has an exact edge-PML obstruction: no positive
coercive energy controlling all displayed variables can be monotone decreasing or
uniformly bounded for all initial data in the edge cases.
